Updated assessment incorporating Financial Stability Report (FSR) context: The statement balances solid growth and low unemployment against “somewhat elevated” inflation and higher two‑sided uncertainty, while keeping the policy rate at 4.25–4.50% and continuing balance‑sheet runoff and facility settings that are restrictive. The April 11, 2025 FSR backdrop points to moderate overall vulnerabilities with persistent stress in commercial real estate (CRE exposures reported through Q4 2024), a gradual uptick in some household delinquencies (for example, autos), and pockets of nonbank funding risk (runnable liabilities and short‑term investment funds), even as bank capital/liquidity remain solid and Treasury market liquidity is generally adequate but sensitive to shocks. Given these stability considerations, the communication skews slightly more cautious than neutral—supporting a “tighter for longer” posture and reducing the likelihood of imminent easing. Net read: mildly hawkish.
